name: Jamiltepec Mixtec
confidence_why: One first-hand description of the tone system, checked against the source; 3 other works consulted do not discuss stress.

tone_statements.citation: Johnson, Audrey F. 1988. A syntactic sketch of Jamiltepec Mixtec. In C. Henry Bradley & Barbara E. Hollenbach (eds.), Studies in the syntax of Mixtecan languages 1 (SIL Publications in Linguistics 83), 11-150. Dallas: SIL & University of Texas at Arlington.
tone_statements.quote: Jamiltepec Mixtec has the following phonological units: voiceless stops and affricates p (rare) ¢ ty ch k kw, prenasalized stops mb (rare) nd ndy ng, … oral vowels ie +a uo, nasalized vowels in en in an un on, tones high (written with acute accent), mid (written with macron), and low (unmarked). … This variety of Mixtec exhibits extensive tone sandhi, in which the basic tone of words is changed after certain other words. In this sketch the basic tones are written.

tone_statements.citation: Johnson, Audrey F. 1983. Cuñi chi cutuhva yo sacuaha yo ta tyaa yo xiñi savi / Leyendo y escribiendo en mixteco (mixteco de Jamiltepec). 2a edición. México, D.F.: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano. 50 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives 12453.)
tone_statements.quote: Muchas pares de palabras en mixteco varían sólo por los tonos. Es decir, se escriben con las mismas letras, pero la voz sube o baja de una manera diferente en cada palabra para darle el significado correcto. [...] Sin embargo, a veces los tiempos de los verbos se pueden confundir. Por eso escribimos un acento (´) en la última vocal del verbo para indicar que se debe pronunciar el tono de tiempo presente, y una rayita (_) debajo de la última vocal para indicar que se debe pronunciar el tono de tiempo pasado. Ejemplos: [...] satá ra 'él está comprando' / sata̱ ra 'él compró'
tone_statements.translation: Many pairs of words in Mixtec differ only in their tones. That is, they are written with the same letters, but the voice rises or falls in a different way in each word to give it the right meaning. [...] However, sometimes the tenses of verbs can be confused. So we write an accent on the last vowel of the verb to show that the present-tense tone must be pronounced, and a small line under the last vowel to show that the past-tense tone must be pronounced. Examples: sata ra 'he is buying' / sata ra 'he bought'.
tone_statements.locator: Lección 2 'Signos del Tiempo de los Verbos', p. 6; cf. Propósito and Lección 4 §2, p. 13

tone.says: Three level tones, high, mid and low, with extensive tone sandhi that changes a word's basic tone after certain words; verb aspect is marked by tone alone in two verb classes.

sources.citation: Penner, Kevin L. 2019. Prosodic structure in Ixtayutla Mixtec: Evidence for the foot. PhD dissertation, University of Alberta. 404 pp. DOI 10.7939/r3-10cf-7t94.
sources.note: About Ixtayutla Mixtec (ISO vmj, neighbouring coastal variety), not Jamiltepec: 'the couplet is the locus of stress assignment.. stress is obligatorily realized in a left-headed, bimoraic structure' (Abstract, p. ii-iii). It cites Johnson 1988 only for the three-tone analysis of Jamiltepec (p. 93) and for Jamiltepec word forms (pp. 80, 261); it makes no claim about Jamiltepec stress.

It is the nearest explicit stress statement to Jamiltepec but cannot be filed as a jami1235 record.

sources.citation: Pensinger, Brenda J. 1974. Diccionario mixteco-español, español-mixteco: mixteco del este de Jamiltepec, pueblo de Chayuco. Serie de Vocabularios y Diccionarios Indígenas 'Mariano Silva y Aceves' 18. México: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano / SEP. 173 pp. (grammar notes pp. 137-146)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. 'La ortografía mixteca' (pp. 137-138) covers letters and 'Los tonos': 'El mixteco es un idioma tonal.. Hay tres niveles de tono en el mixteco de Chayuco' (alto, medio, bajo). The word 'acento' does not occur in the grammar notes. NB this dictionary describes Chayuco Mixtec ('mixteco del este de Jamiltepec, pueblo de Chayuco', ISO mih, Glottolog chay1249), not Jamiltepec proper; the earlier scan note that called it the Jamiltepec dictionary is confirmed as 'tone described, no stress statement' but for the Chayuco variety.
Nothing; references are only Ethnologue entries for mxt and mih.

sources.citation: Stark Campbell, Sara, Andrea Johnson Peterson & Filiberto Lorenzo Cruz (comps.). 1986. Diccionario mixteco de San Juan Colorado. Serie de Vocabularios y Diccionarios Indígenas 'Mariano Silva y Aceves' 29. México: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; the 'Gramática mixteca' §0.2 describes three tones (alto, medio, bajo) and their nine/seven combinations on disyllabic words; 'acento' is used only for the written accent marks. San Juan Colorado Mixtec (ISO mjc) is a separate ISO language, but Johnson 1988:17 lists San Juan Colorado among towns speaking 'dialects closely related to that of Jamiltepec'.

sources.note: First-hand practical statement: many word pairs differ only by tone (the voice rises or falls differently); verb tense (present vs past) is distinguished by tone alone, so the orthography writes an acute on the last vowel for the present-tense tone and an underline for the past-tense tone (grammatical tone); Leccion 4 sec. 2 (p. 13) adds further lexical minimal pairs 'que se pueden confundir por los tonos' (gente/vida, fuego/tierra, luna/quien/nosotros). No tone inventory is given (Johnson 1988:18 gives high, mid, low + extensive tone sandhi).

sources.citation: Johnson, Audrey F. 1986. Jamiltepec Mixtec word list. Unpublished manuscript, 16 pp. Bartholomew Collection of Unpublished Materials, SIL International - Mexico Branch. SIL Language & Culture Archives 56672.
sources.note: No prose. 16 typescript pages of c. 50 entries each (c. 810 lines): Mixtec forms with English glosses, tone marked three ways (acute accent, underlined vowel, unmarked) with no key in the manuscript; the published sketch it fed (Johnson 1988:18) writes high = acute, mid = macron, low = unmarked, so the underline most plausibly renders the macron (mid) - an inference, not stated. Aspect pairs differ by tone marking alone (ms. p. 2: chitá CON-sing / chita̱ COM-sing, chitó CON-know / chito̱ COM-know, chi̱sókó CON-be-hungry / chi̱soko COM-be-hungry), matching the present/past tone signs taught in…
